title: Adventure Games: Discover the Story: The Dungeon: The Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zrRTPvOBEnU

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens with the only complaint he can find: the game is genuinely called Adventure Games: Discover the Story: The Dungeon, about the most generic name in board gaming. Everything after that is praise. Kosmos built this line adjacent to their EXIT escape rooms, but where those demand hardcore puzzle-cracking, this series is interested in narrative discovery — closer to a Sierra or LucasArts adventure with the esoterica stripped out.

The structure is dead simple. Four characters each carry a single trait — attentive, skilled, knowledgeable, strong — and which one matters depends on who the passage happens to be about, which gives them more presence than one word should. Nobody dies; you lose health, and lost health means a worse ending. Two card decks and an adventure book do the rest: move a meeple to a numbered location, read the entry, then combine item cards by reading their numbers lowest-first to hunt for a matching passage. If the passage doesn't exist, the combination was meaningless.

Chapters two and three permanently alter the dungeon — floods, collapses — pushing you forward past content you'll never see. Daniel reckons two good plays per group, at roughly $8 per hour of entertainment, and a game you can then loan onward indefinitely.

----

Would you rather a narrative adventure that gives you two brilliant plays and then travels around your friend group, or one that stretches thinner but stays on your shelf?
